name: Clonidine
lead: Clonidine is a prescription alpha-2 adrenergic agonist that lowers sympathetic nervous system activity. It is approved for high blood pressure, and extended-release forms are approved for ADHD in children and adolescents [1][2]. Clinicians also use it off-label for conditions with an appearance component, including flushing in rosacea and menopausal hot flashes, and some prescribers use it at bedtime for sleep problems [8].

In looksmaxxing-adjacent forums, clonidine comes up in a stress-and-sleep framing rather than as a direct cosmetic: one looksmax.org thread reposts a Ray Peat-community user's suggestion to combine pregnenolone, clonidine and cyproheptadine for stress and attention problems [3]. Bodybuilding forums such as T Nation discuss it in two other contexts: as a drug some growth-hormone users mention for water retention, and as a sedating agent that some members say increases growth hormone pulses during sleep [16][17]. People who follow the stress reasoning treat lower stress and better sleep as a route to better skin, energy and presentation. No published trial has tested such a combination or clonidine for appearance outcomes.

Common adverse effects on the label include dry mouth, drowsiness and dizziness, and the label warns against abrupt discontinuation because of rebound hypertension [1]. It is prescription-only in the US, UK, Canada, EU and Australia [8].

paras: The label lists treatment of hypertension, alone or with other antihypertensives [1]. Wikipedia describes it as a second-line antihypertensive because of sedation and dry mouth, typically reserved for resistant hypertension or hypertensive emergencies [8]. Grokipedia reports that clonidine was developed as a nasal decongestant, then repurposed after its blood-pressure-lowering and sedating effects were seen in early human testing [2]. A Veterans Affairs study compared six antihypertensive drugs including clonidine with placebo [4]; a 1980 review also covers its use in hypertension [15].

Extended-release clonidine is FDA-approved for ADHD in ages 6 to 17, alone or with stimulants [2]. It is a non-stimulant, second-line option, according to Wikipedia [8]. A network meta-analysis of ADHD drugs includes clonidine among non-stimulant options [5]. A Cochrane network meta-analysis of smoking-cessation drugs also considered clonidine among other therapies [6].

Wikipedia lists further uses: easing symptoms of opioid, alcohol, benzodiazepine and nicotine withdrawal, perioperative pain and sedation, and off-label use for tics, PTSD-related hyperarousal, anxiety, restless legs syndrome, migraine, menopausal hot flashes and rosacea flushing [8]. A 1978 randomized trial reported that clonidine blocked acute opiate-withdrawal symptoms [14].

Wikipedia notes that clonidine was formerly used in a growth hormone stimulation test and in a suppression test for pheochromocytoma, and that it is sometimes used at bedtime for sleep problems in people taking it for ADHD [8]. It reports low abuse potential compared with psychostimulants [8].

Clonidine stimulates alpha-2 receptors in the brainstem, reducing sympathetic outflow, heart rate and peripheral resistance [2]. Early work reported inhibition of noradrenergic and serotonergic neurons in the brain [7]. Wikipedia adds that it acts on imidazoline receptors and that alpha-2A activation in the prefrontal cortex supports attention and working memory, which is the proposed basis for its ADHD use [8].

According to Wikipedia, oral bioavailability is 70 to 80 percent and 60 to 70 percent with a transdermal patch; oral onset is roughly 30 to 60 minutes with blood-pressure effects lasting up to about 8 hours. Reported half-life estimates range from 6 to 23 hours, around 12 to 16 hours for immediate release, longer in kidney failure. Metabolism is mainly hepatic via CYP2D6, with about 72 percent excreted in urine [8].

The label reports dry mouth in about 40 of 100 patients, drowsiness in about 33, dizziness in about 16, and constipation and sedation in about 10 each [1]. Sudden cessation has resulted in nervousness, agitation, headache, tremor and a rapid rise in blood pressure [1]. Grokipedia notes hypotension, bradycardia and angioedema as more serious risks [2]. Wikipedia reports skin dermatitis in roughly 15 to 20 percent of patch users, high physical dependence and rebound hypertension that can be severe after abrupt withdrawal, which is why tapering is used [8].

A review titled Clonidine toxicity revisited covers overdose [9], and Wikipedia notes that in children central nervous system depression does not clearly track with the ingested dose and that naloxone can reverse overdose [8]. A randomized trial reported that clonidine increased a marker of bone resorption in humans [10].

Wikipedia also lists heart block and other bradyarrhythmias, syncope, mood changes and, rarely, hallucinations among less common effects, and says use in pregnancy and breastfeeding is not recommended without caution because the drug passes into breast milk [8].

Wikipedia dates the patent to 1961 and medical use to 1966, with hypertension as the first indication under the Catapres name [8]. Grokipedia and the extended-release label cite 1974 as the US introduction year [1][2]. Clonidine was reported to have arisen from imidazoline research and to have been repurposed from a nasal decongestant after unexpected blood-pressure and sedative effects [2]. Extended-release clonidine was approved for ADHD in the US in the 2010s, with Grokipedia reporting a 2010 approval for Kapvay and a 2024 liquid form [2].

Wikipedia reports that clonidine was patented in 1961, introduced for medical use in 1966 under the Catapres name for hypertension, and is now sold as a generic [8]. The 1993 Veterans Affairs cooperative study compared six antihypertensive agents including clonidine with placebo in men [4], and a 1978 Lancet trial reported that it blocked acute opiate-withdrawal symptoms, a use that later became established in withdrawal management [14][8].

In 2023 clonidine was the 82nd most-prescribed drug in the US, with over 8 million prescriptions, according to Wikipedia [8]. It is sold under many brand names, including combination products with diuretics [8]. In looksmaxxing forums it is mentioned occasionally in Ray Peat-influenced stress and attention threads, where members cite their own experience rather than trials [3].

Wikipedia lists brand names including Catapres, Kapvay and Onyda XR, and combination products with chlortalidone or bendroflumethiazide [8]. It is also being studied as an adjunct in borderline personality disorder with comorbid PTSD, though Wikipedia notes the trials are small and larger placebo-controlled studies are needed [8].

Trials of clonidine are summarized in meta-analyses for ADHD and smoking cessation and in the 1993 Veterans Affairs hypertension comparison [4][5][6]. The 2018 Lancet Psychiatry network meta-analysis compared amphetamines, atomoxetine, bupropion, clonidine, guanfacine, methylphenidate and modafinil with each other or placebo, with efficacy measured by teacher and clinician ratings of core ADHD symptoms and tolerability by dropouts due to side effects [5]. A 1999 meta-analysis addressed clonidine specifically for ADHD symptoms [11]. A phase 4 trial registered by the manufacturer enrolled 135 children and adolescents to test extended-release clonidine in ADHD [12]. A registered study of 82 people examined stress neuromodulators in decision-making under risk [13]. No studies were found testing clonidine, alone or in the forum combination described above, for stress-related appearance outcomes.

A looksmax.org thread reposts advice from a Ray Peat-influenced forum user suggesting pregnenolone, clonidine and cyproheptadine to lower stress and address attention problems [3]. The reposted material also discusses growth hormone, which Peat-community writers describe as undesirable at high levels [3]. This is anecdotal forum advice and not a studied regimen.

On T Nation, one thread on injected growth hormone includes an account of a user who also took clonidine for water retention, and a later poster on a 'HGH cut' thread says clonidine and the related drug guanfacine, while heavily sedating, both increase growth hormone pulses during sleep [16][17]. These are individual forum accounts; the cited studies of clonidine examine hypertension, ADHD, withdrawal and smoking cessation rather than physique or appearance [4][5][6][14].

lore.intro: Clonidine surfaces on looksmax.org in a repost of a Ray Peat-community stress and attention protocol [3]. Discussion centres on stress control rather than appearance directly.

claims.claim: Pregnenolone plus clonidine plus cyproheptadine lowers stress and treats attention problems.
claims.believers: A forum user quoted in a looksmax.org thread said ADD and low motivation point to low dopamine and that this trio addresses stress [3].
claims.experts: Clonidine is approved for hypertension and (extended-release) ADHD; no published study has tested this combination [1][2][5].

claims.claim: Clonidine helps keep stress under control.
claims.believers: Ray Peat-community users say stress is a core driver of poor skin, energy and motivation, and mention clonidine among tools for lowering it [3].
claims.experts: Clonidine lowers sympathetic outflow and is approved for hypertension and ADHD [1][2]; its sedation and dry mouth are among the most common effects [1]. No published trial tests it as a general stress aid for healthy people.

claims.claim: Clonidine raises growth hormone during sleep, which helps body composition
claims.believers: A T Nation poster says clonidine and guanfacine both increase growth hormone pulses during sleep.[17]
claims.experts: Wikipedia notes clonidine's historical use in a growth hormone stimulation test; no published study in this record tests it for body composition or appearance.[8]

claims.claim: Clonidine helps flushing and hot flashes that affect appearance
claims.believers: Clinical and online discussions mention it for rosacea flushing.[8]
claims.experts: Wikipedia lists rosacea flushing and menopausal hot flashes as off-label uses; it also reports dry mouth, sedation and low blood pressure as common effects.[8]

card.summary: A blood-pressure and ADHD prescription drug that surfaces in forum stress stacks; nothing tests it for looks.
card.note: Rebound hypertension if stopped abruptly; dry mouth, drowsiness and low blood pressure are common.

quick.overview:
Clonidine is a prescription alpha-2 agonist used for high blood pressure, and in extended-release form for ADHD in children and adolescents.

On looksmax.org one thread reposts a suggestion to combine it with pregnenolone and cyproheptadine for stress. No published study has tested that.
quick.mechanism: It activates alpha-2 receptors in the brainstem, lowering sympathetic nervous system output, heart rate and vascular resistance.
quick.risks: The label reports dry mouth, drowsiness, dizziness and constipation, and warns that abrupt discontinuation can cause rebound high blood pressure. Prescription-only.

chain: Alpha-2 stimulation reduces sympathetic nervous system outflow
Forum users describe calmer stress response and, for some, easier sleep
Lower stress and better rest are discussed as supporting skin, energy and presentation
angle.text: Clonidine reaches appearance discussions through stress control and, in medical practice, through reduction of flushing episodes. Forum users who use the stress route describe it as part of a broader stress-and-attention protocol; the evidence for appearance outcomes specifically is absent from published trials.
